key_insight: A solver-guided LLM can learn to choose the best MIP formulation for each inventory-allocation instance, rather than relying on one fixed formulation for all cases.
engineering_relevance: This enables more adaptive warehouse planning by matching OR model structure to instance-specific conditions like demand concentration, imbalance, and forecast volatility.
method: Build a candidate library of solver-executable MIP formulations, each representing a different allocation priority.
Train the selector with balanced expert-conditioned supervised fine-tuning, then add solver-informed IPO preferences and GRPO rewards from historical instance quality gaps.
Use per-instance expert-score metadata to reward sampled responses during policy optimization.
evidence_signal: On JD.com multi-warehouse inventory allocation instances, GRPO raised Hit Ratio@1 from 21.45% to 50.42% and Hit Ratio@2 from 70.47% to 82.31%, improving allocation accuracy by 12.57 percentage points over the incumbent baseline.
watch_item: Performance depends on reliable solver evaluations and a well-curated expert library, so deployment may be sensitive to data shift or missing formulation coverage.
paper_title: Large Language Model for Operations Research Formulation Selection in Multi-Warehouse Inventory Allocation
